author: Sam Graham
title: Midterm races set for Virginia's 5th, 6th and 9th congressional districts - NewsBreak
text:
By Sam Graham ,
1 hours ago
ROANOKE, Va. ( WFXR ) — As one election ends, another begins as Virginia’s year of voting turns toward its final act.
The Commonwealth’s redistricting referendum, ultimately struck down by the state Supreme Court, sent voters to the polls in April, with early voting beginning in early March.
By the time the ink was dry on the court decision, early voting for the August midterms was heating up.
Now, with primary season officially in the rearview mirror, candidates are left with less than three months until election day to campaign, and just over a month before the early voting period opens.
That’s why if you were looking for projected VA-05 Democratic nominee Tom Perriello on Wednesday, you would not find him celebrating his decisive unofficial primary victory, but rallying his voting base in Lynchburg for the home stretch.
IN ROANOKE: City Council candidates, Mayor Cobb react to Democratic Primary Perriello, who formerly served VA-05 in the U.S. House of Representatives from 2009-2011, emerged out of a three-candidate primary Tuesday night with nearly 80 percent of the vote, setting up a race between himself and incumbent Republican congressman John McGuire in November.
“It’s 90 days to decide whether this district is going to get a fighter again,” said Perriello. “Someone who cares about this place and listens to families here and actually votes their conscience. We deserve that back. Clearly, we’re not going to get that from John McGuire.”
McGuire also had to earn his party’s nomination to defend his seat, but did so comfortably, claiming the projected win with 84 percent of the vote to challenger Melanie Lucero’s 15 percent.
The congressman said he believes a tighter fight awaits him in the general election, framing his own race and this fall’s midterms as a whole as a battle between “common sense and communism crazy.”
“It’s going to be a tough fight,” said McGuire. “But if we put our differences aside, we work together as a team, we’re going to keep the fifth district red. We’re going to win the midterms, and we’re going to continue to work together to make America great again, for all Americans.”
In VA-09, incumbent Republican had nothing to do on primary night but wait to see who would be challenging him in November.
It appears that designation belongs to Democrat Joy Powers, declared the primary winner with 51 percent of the vote in a three-candidate race.
Joy Powers wins primary to face Morgan Griffith in November VA-09 is one of the toughest Republican strongholds in the Commonwealth, but Powers says she’s prepared to challenge that reputation.
“I came into this race determined to make this a rural Democratic race,” said Powers. “This is one of the most rural districts east of the [Mississippi River]. And they deserve rural representation. We had people vote in this Democratic primary who have never voted in a Democratic primary and who are not Democrats just because they believe in this campaign.”
In a statement provided to WFXR News Wednesday, Griffith said he’s not prepared to give up an inch of the district seat he has held for 15 years, a seat he defended in 2024 by claiming 72 percent of the vote in the general election:
“My focus is where it has been since the people of Virginia’s Ninth District first sent me to Washington: farmers and agriculture jobs, lower energy bills, better roads and broadband, care for our veterans, and a secure border. I have worked with President Trump to deliver American energy dominance, tax relief for working families, and an end to the policies that spent a generation telling Southwest and Southside Virginia its way of life was a problem to be managed. I intend to earn every vote in every locality of this district, and I look forward to continuing to serve the people of the Ninth.”
The VA-06 race was set well before primary election day after all challengers dropped out, clearing the way for voters to choose between incumbent Republican congressman Ben Cline and New York Times bestselling author Beth Macy.
Election day is Tuesday, November 3.
